minutes.headline: Committee voted to send a letter asking that remaining ARPA funds go mostly to Marshall Park, plus a plow/sander and turf field.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a presentation tying social-emotional learning, equity and the strategy for continuous improvement together, and discussed how to approach a non-discrimination policy. It also discussed a letter on use of remaining ARPA funds and a letter supporting the Primary School project, then moved five fiscal policies through second and third reads. Minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Chair invited public comment; none was offered at the opening.
A speaker thanked the committee for communication and noted the sign in front of the primary school.

decisions.decision: The committee will send a letter asking that the majority of remaining ARPA funds go to Marshall Park and add the plow sander and turf field if funds allow.
Chair and superintendent authorized to move the Primary School letter forward, with fine-tuning of the phase breakdown and answers on heat damage and operating costs.
Non-discrimination policy: policy subcommittee to meet Friday with the school attorney and seek teacher input; the whole committee to weigh in on guiding principles first.
Strategy for continuous improvement to be revised over the summer and brought back to the committee in early fall.
May 3 meeting may be moved if the attorney is available nearby; chair will notify members.

what_happened.line: The committee voted by voice to send a letter asking that most remaining ARPA funds go to Marshall Park, adding a plow/sander and a turf field if money allows.
The chair and superintendent were authorized to move the Primary School project letter forward, pending work on the phase breakdown, heat damage and operating costs.
Five fiscal policies, including the grants policy, went through second and third reads; the minutes record the outcomes of these votes as not audible.
The non-discrimination policy goes to the policy subcommittee, which will meet with the school attorney and seek teacher input after the full committee weighs in on principles.
The strategy for continuous improvement is to be revised over the summer and brought back in early fall.

why_it_matters: The ARPA letter is a request on how leftover one-time federal money is spent, so it bears on which capital needs get funded without drawing on the tax levy.
The Primary School project letter and its open questions on phasing and operating costs bear on a building project residents may later be asked to fund.
